definition: A quantity that is stored and transferred but never created or destroyed; it is a scalar, measured in joules (J).
One of the ways energy is held: internal (thermal), kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic (strain), chemical, nuclear or electrostatic.
Energy in the kinetic store of a moving object; for mass $m$ moving at speed $v$ it is $E_\text{k} = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2$.

Energy in the gravitational potential store of an object because of its height; near the Earth's surface, raising a mass $m$ by a vertical height $\Delta h$ increases it by $\Delta E_\text{p} = mg\Delta h$.
The total energy of the particles in an object (their kinetic and potential energy), also called its thermal store; heating the object increases it.
The principle that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred from one store to another, so the total amount of energy stays the same.
A diagram that shows energy transfers as arrows whose widths are proportional to the energy they carry, usually with useful energy going straight on and wasted energy branching off.
